title: Left exactness of ordinary completed coefficient pullback
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, and schemes T,W in an independent scheme universe. Use their small pro-etale sites and completed coefficient sheaves B_T,B_W. Equip g:T → W with the projection-defined completedRingMap of [lem-tw-completed-coefficient-ringed-coherence], and let g_B^* be the specified sheaf-module left adjoint of its sectionwise direct image [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Then g_B^* preserves finite limits. The coefficient and scheme universes are independent. Coefficients and their quotients are those of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]; sites and scheme morphisms are [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

proof.text: Apply Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing to the actual lifted finite quotient tower. Shrink each finite carrier to the scheme universe and use the finite-test-object construction and its preserved geometric limit from the finite-tower representation module. Transport the finite-constant representability isomorphism through ULift and sheafification to the independent coefficient universe. The lifted Yoneda comparison then shows that the constructed set inverse image preserves this tower limit. Forgetting commutative rings commutes with inverse image, since the pointwise Kan-extension indices are filtered and forgetting preserves filtered colimits and sheafification. Reflect the preserved tower limit to ring sheaves. Each constant-ring comparison is invertible by uniqueness of the constant-sheaf adjunction. The completed coefficient sheaf is a limit cone on this tower: verify it after forgetting to RingCat, where it is the defining limit. The completedMap_projection equations make completedRingMap a morphism between the two limiting cones, so it is invertible.

Use the preceding coefficient isomorphism and the unit compatibility of the forgetful inverse-image comparison to present the underlying set sheaf of B_T as inverse image of B_W, with exactly the structural unit specified by directRingMap. The general-universe SignedLine inverse-image adjunction identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of the specified module pullback with constructed abelian inverse image. Set and abelian inverse image preserve finite limits by flatness of pro-etale base change and exactness of the relevant filtered colimits. Module forgetting preserves and reflects finite limits. Reflect this preservation to the specified pull functor, unfolding its recorded adjoint instance.
